To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the proposed metrics can be used to evaluate the reliability of a wide range of RL algorithms, 2) the metrics are useful in comparing algorithms, 3) the metrics and statistical tools are available in the open-source library, 4) there is a large variance in the performance of the tested algorithms on the metrics.

(1) the metrics are effective in measuring the reliability of algorithms, (2) the metrics are sensitive enough to detect differences between algorithms, (3) the metrics can help us identify the causes of differences in the algorithms’ reliability, and (4) the metrics can be used to compare algorithms across different environments.

(i) the metrics are useful and can be used in many different ways; (ii) they provide insights about the reliability of different algorithms and environments; and (iii) the statistical tests are reliable and can be used to compare different algorithms and environments.

the following question: how do we evaluate and compare the reliability of different RL algorithms?

the metrics and statistical tests are useful for evaluating reliability in RL algorithms and that they are complementary to the standard metrics that are used in RL research.
